# Ox Alpha — max

> A visually confident, data-complete Pokedex whose static index layer is the real achievement and whose detail layer is where it comes apart. scripts/generate-data.mjs is a properly engineered fetcher (backoff retry, 404 passthrough, 24-way pool) emitting seven key-minified indexes that I verified complete and correct end to end — 1,025 contiguous base species plus 326 forms, 937 moves, 373 abilities, 2,223 items, 68 berries, an exact 18-type chart — so browse, search, eight-key sort, type/gen/legendary/mythical faceting, the type matrix, team analysis and compare are all zero-network and all arithmetically right. Against that, the detail route re-fetches over the wire data the app already shipped (AbilityCard and MoveDetailModal both ignore the resident ABILITIES/MOVES indexes), fires GET /pokemon-species/0 on every load because `speciesId ?? 0` defeats its own null guard, and carries three stale-state defects from the same missing-reset discipline: the cry button keeps the previous species' Audio, the flavor-text index is never reset so the counter goes out of range, and the evolution view resolves nodes against a map keyed on Pokemon names rather than species names, giving ~21 species placeholder art and 404 links. The documented regeneration command crashes on four null-firmness berries before writing types.json and generations.json — both hard imports — so the pipeline that produced the app's defining asset cannot be re-run; the shipped data came from three undocumented patch scripts in an unrecorded order. Accessibility below the aria-label layer is unbuilt: no Escape, focus trap or role=dialog on any of four modals, no keyboard path to any move detail, no prefers-reduced-motion despite two infinite animations. Adjudicating the audit: I accepted every downgrade it argued (national-dex, artwork, moves-dex and theming are complete-and-correct 2s rather than best-in-class; cries, evolution and flavor-entries have confirmed wrong-output paths), extended the same evidence to forms, and rejected its robustness upgrade to 8 — its own findings elsewhere show three user-visible wrong-output defects, not four cosmetic ones.

## Strengths

- The static index prebuild is real and verified complete at full scale — 1,351 dex entries, 937 moves, 373 abilities, 2,223 items, 68 berries, 9 generations — making every browse, filter, sort and analysis surface zero-network
- Type effectiveness is exactly right: utils.ts:33-43 multiplies across all defending slots for true 4×/0.25×/0× results, off a types.json I checked row-by-row against the canonical Gen6+ chart, with one implementation shared by the detail grid, compare, team analysis and the 18×18 matrix
- All 326 alternate forms ship as first-class browsable entries with working detail pages, and PokemonDetail.tsx:36 correctly resolves a form's species via species.url rather than naively reusing the form id
- Motion is used with intent rather than decoration — capped index-staggered card entrance, a hero spring keyed on id+shiny so the shiny toggle re-animates, width-animated stat bars with per-stat delay, spring modals via AnimatePresence — plus skeletons at three granularities
- Genuine responsive engineering: the moves table progressively drops columns and substitutes a mobile-only effect line, rather than just reflowing a grid
- Layered, non-decorative error handling — query-error page on the detail route, artwork→sprite image fallback that demonstrably rescues form sprites PokeAPI lacks artwork for, try/caught localStorage reads, caught audio play() rejection, SPA _redirects for deep links

## Weaknesses

- Three stale-state defects from the same missing-reset discipline, all reachable by ordinary detail→detail navigation to a cached target: the cry button plays the previous species' audio indefinitely, the flavor counter renders out-of-range values like '4/2', and neither has a key or reset effect
- EvolutionView resolves nodes via DEX_BY_NAME.get(species.name) against a map keyed on Pokemon names — 21 of 22 sampled species miss, so Espurr→Meowstic, Frillish→Jellicent, Honedge→Aegislash and ~18 more lines render placeholder icons linking to 404s
- Only evolution_details[0] is ever rendered, so 44 of 484 links hide their modern method behind a retired one (Leafeon shows 'at Eterna Forest', never the Leaf Stone), and branching families are laid out in one flat row that reads as linear
- The detail route re-fetches over the network data the app already ships: AbilityCard issues useAbility per ability and MoveDetailModal issues useMoveDetail, while ABILITIES (373 entries with effect text) and MOVES (937 with type/power/acc/pp/effect) sit resident and unread
- `npm run generate:data` — the single documented pipeline command — throws on `b.firmness.name` for four null-firmness berries before writing types.json and generations.json, both hard imports in data.ts, so a clean regeneration leaves the build unable to compile; the shipped data required three undocumented patch scripts with fetch/pool logic triplicated across them
- Every detail page fires GET /pokemon-species/0 → 404 because PokemonDetail.tsx:37 passes `speciesId ?? 0` through a guard testing `!= null` — the app's one measured console error, self-inflicted
- Accessibility stops at aria-labels: four modals with no role=dialog, aria-modal, focus trap, scroll lock or Escape; move details reachable only by mouse via bare `<tr onClick>`; no aria-pressed on any filter toggle; no prefers-reduced-motion despite two infinite animations and a 5s auto-advancing text rotation with no pause
- No sorting on any surface but the browse page, so a 937-row moves dex and a 2,223-item grid can only be filtered; items have no detail view at all and berries have no search
- The 326 form rows carry l:false/m:false and inherit their base species' generation, so Legendary+Forms silently omits every Mega and legendary form, and Megas file under Gen 1-3
- A copy-pasted GitHub Octocat path ships as the Psychic type icon in production, rendered inside every Psychic badge app-wide

## Standout

The build-time data pipeline: a retrying, concurrency-pooled fetcher that emits seven key-minified indexes covering the entire PokeAPI surface, verified correct at full scale, so browse, search, eight-key sort, faceting, the 18×18 type matrix, compare and team analysis all run with zero network — the shame being that the detail route then goes back over the wire for data already sitting in the bundle, and the command that regenerates it all crashes two files short.

## Vendored source

The source in this directory is the code the model wrote, copied verbatim from [its repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-ox-alpha-max) minus `node_modules`, build output, and generated data.

Canonical history and issues live in the [original repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-ox-alpha-max). This is a scored snapshot for the benchmark.
